https://www.kotatv.com/2026/07/30/justic.text: Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - The U.S. Department of Justice is looking to revoke the naturalized citizenship of ten people, including a former Rapid City Catholic priest. Marcin Garbacz, 47, is a native of Poland and became a legal permanent U.S. resident in 2008 and a naturalized citizen in 2014. Garbacz was accused of stealing about $269,000 in collections from three parishes in the Rapid City Catholic Diocese and was convicted of wire fraud and money laundering in 2020. He also pleaded guilty in 2021 to shooting videos of a 17 year old boy in the shower on a church trip to Poland. In the filing, the Justice Department says Garbacz illegally procured his citizenship by lacking the good moral character needed, providing false testimony during the naturalization process and concealing material facts and willful misrepresentations. Garbacz is currently in federal prison in Colorado and is scheduled for release in March of 2029. See a spelling or grammatical error in our story? Please click here to report it. https://www.dw.com/en/guatemala-says-it-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JB3z Immigration experts say that by sending Mexicans through Guatemala or other third countries, the US wants to make it more difficult for them to cross back into its territory [FILE: Jan 23, 2025] Image: Christian Torres/Anadolu/picture alliance Advertisement The United States has deported and sent some 2,300 Mexicans to Guatemala this year in a shifting Trump administration practice that Mexico opposes. Mexican deportees from the US, until recently, were largely sent directly back to their country, with only a few arriving in other countries. On Wednesday, Guatemalan President Bernardo Arevalo confirmed that 2,284 Mexicans deported from the US have arrived in his Central American country so far this year. "They are arriving in planes of Guatemalan ‌returnees," Arevalo ⁠said ⁠in a televised interview. He said the deported Mexicans are arriving in a "transit stopover" before being taken to Mexico as part of an "arrangement" with Mexico's government. Arevalo said the Mexican deportees were transferred to their home country within 24 hours, with Mexico or the US covering the transportation costs. What has Mexico said about the US deportations? On Thursday, Mexico's Foreign Ministry voiced its objection to the US practice and said that it was coordinating with the countries involved to ensure the safe repatriation of its nationals. "The Mexican government has expressed its opposition to this practice to US authorities and has reiterated that every Mexican citizen has the right to enter the country," it asserted. The ministry did not give any details on the number of cases or costs. What is the US' third country deportation policy under Trump? As per international accords, migrants may be sent to third countries if their home country rejects them or if it is unsafe for them to be sent back. Otherwise, they should be directly deported back to their country of citizenship. The Trump administration has however been using third-country deportations to send back migrants, striking bilateral agreements with several countries, including Mexico, to receive migrants from other countries. Immigration experts say that by sending Mexicans through Guatemala or other third countries, thereby moving them farther from the US-Mexico border, the US wants to make it more difficult for them to cross back into its territory. Mexicans sent back via Honduras: reports According to reports, some Mexicans deported by the US were also being sent to Honduras . The Associated Press cited official documents from Honduras as showing that 82 Mexican deportees from the US arrived in the city of San Pedro Sula aboard two flights last week, with an additional 35 who were due to arrive Thursday. There was no immediate statement from the Honduran government. According to the 'Third Country Deportation Watch' tracker of Human Rights First and Refugees International, Honduras received 165 Mexicans by mid-July and another 37 Mexicans have been deported from the US to Honduras by mid-August so far. In a press release this week , the organizations deemed the third country transfers by the US government as an "opaque and cruel system," saying that "thousands of individuals have been subjected to arbitrary detention, family separations, and chain refoulement in third countries." Read Romanian Foreign Ministry hosts 4th edition of international programme on countering disinformation Romania, Bucharest September 13, 2026 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Romania, in partnership with Romania’s International Development Cooperation Agency (RoAid), is hosting the fourth edition of the training programme titled “Building Resilience to Disinformation in a Changing Communication Environment” in Bucharest from September 7 to 11, 2026. The week-long programme brings together international participants, diplomats, strategic communication experts, government officials, media professionals, and civil society representatives to exchange best practices and strengthen institutional responses to foreign information manipulation and interference (FIMI). The opening session at the Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs featured welcome addresses by Clara Staicu, State Secretary for European Affairs, Middle East and Africa at the Romanian MFA, and Director of Public Diplomacy of RoAid. Addressing delegates during the opening, the leadership of the Ministry emphasized that combating disinformation and information manipulation has become a critical shared challenge for governments, institutions, and citizens worldwide. The initiative aims to provide a collaborative roundtable format where participants can share operational experience, practical tools, and whole-of-society strategies to safeguard information integrity and public trust. The training curriculum covers key institutional policies and frameworks, including briefings on Romanian development cooperation, European Union initiatives, and NATO security communication strategies delivered by senior foreign affairs and defence officials. Participants are examining diverse case studies on foreign information manipulation across regions, featuring presentations and insights from the European External Action Service Stratcom Africa Task Force, France’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Poland’s Department for Strategic Communication and Countering Disinformation, and Moldova’s Center for Strategic Communication and Countering Disinformation. Practical components of the programme focus on practical debunking methods, media education, and the crucial role of fact-checking in safeguarding information integrity. The schedule also incorporates direct study visits and institutional exchanges, including sessions at Radio France International Romania, the Cotroceni Presidential Palace, and the Dimitrie Gusti National Village Museum. The programme concludes on Friday, September 11, with an official certificate awarding ceremony led by representatives of the Romanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and RoAidn and Daniela Dobre, Director General of RoAid. The event underscores Romania’s sustained commitment to fostering international partnerships, technical capacity-building, and democratic resilience against modern information threats. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/9.text: Listen (6 mins) Save Share ‘A Ceuta-style surge is possible’: Border tensions on NATO’s eastern flank on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Latvian President Edgars Rinkevics looks through night vision goggles during a visit to the Piedruja, Latvia border crossing with Belarus, August 17, 2026 [Ints Kalnins/Reuters] By Agnieszka Pikulicka-Wilczewska Published On 9 Oct 2026 9 Oct 2026 Masked and armed men attempted to cross into Latvia from Belarus alongside 20 undocumented migrants on Monday. “The (masked) escorts of the illegal migrants, who were located on the Belarusian side, were armed, issued threats to … soldiers, and also actively urged and drove the migrant group toward Latvia,” Janis Dombrava, Latvia’s interior minister, said on Tuesday. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Is Europe preparing for a wider war with Russia? list 2 of 4 Russia warns NATO of possible nuclear response if Kaliningrad is cut off list 3 of 4 Latvia’s governing party wins parliamentary elections by wide margin list 4 of 4 Belarus frees 25 political prisoners in return for US sanctions relief end of list The group was stopped by the military. Later, masked men managed to enter Latvia, destroying an electrical box and stealing surveillance cameras before returning to Belarus – an act of sabotage orchestrated by the country, according to Latvian officials. It was not clear if the second incident involved the same masked men as the first. “Unlike many previous incidents, this time the provocation was particularly demonstrative and aggressive,” said Dombrava. Since 2021, Belarus, Russia’s ally, has used migration as a tool to destabilise NATO’s eastern flank. It shares borders with Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia – the latter considered Europe’s weakest link. “The crisis at the EU [European Union] border with Belarus has been ongoing for five years. The situation in Latvia has been deteriorating since May of this year,” Bartosz Chmielewski, Baltics expert from the Poland-based Centre for Eastern Studies told Al Jazeera. “There has been a steady rise in border violations and the number of people crossing.” In September and October, “the number of border violations has already reached 12,000, a level equal to the total for the entire previous year”, he said. Advertisement According to Olevs Nikers, the Latvian president of the Baltic Security Foundation, “A Ceuta-style surge is physically possible, and we should plan for it.” He was referring to the recent crossing of tens of thousands of people from Morocco to Spain. “But sustained low-level pressure may be the more effective strategy. It creates exhaustion, budget pressure and friction between allies. Poland’s renewed controls on its border with Lithuania are already an example of this.” He noted that Lithuania’s border with Belarus is four times longer than Latvia’s 173km (107 miles), yet pressure has been concentrated in Latvia. “This looks less like spontaneous migration than a deliberate instrument, adjusted to test the neighbour perceived as most vulnerable,” Nikers said. Any migration pressure from Belarus may cause bureaucratic chaos. Latvia, with a population of 1.8 million, would struggle with the reception, processing and providing medical aid to potential asylum seekers, he said. The Latvia border with Belarus near Piedruja, Latvia [File: Ints Kalnins/Reuters] According to the Polish Border Guard, in 2021, almost 40,000 people tried to cross the border from Belarus. Thousands more crossings of undocumented people were never recorded. Before Russia’s war in Ukraine began in 2022, Belarus built a system – including travel agencies, plane connections and visa programmes – encouraging migrants seeking a better life to cross into the European Union from the east. The scheme targeted people from the Global South, or Latin America, Africa and much of Asia. According to experts, the system has since been dismantled, but Belarus is still pressing migration when it can. “A sudden influx of several thousand people into Latgale in winter would become a humanitarian and political problem before it became a border-security problem,” Nikers added. Out of all of NATO’s eastern flank countries, Latvia seems the least prepared for provocations coming from the east. “Until now, Latvia remained on the sidelines, as the pressure was primarily focused on Poland and Lithuania. Now it finds itself in the spotlight, partly because it is unprepared, its border infrastructure is inadequate, and the resources of the border guard – even with military support – are dwindling,” Chmielewski said. “Latvia struggles to execute major infrastructure projects … It shares the shortest border with Belarus, but has been unable to complete the necessary infrastructure there; this is due both to the challenging terrain and the state’s limited operational capacity.” Other experts said the migration pressure from Belarus might be a response to recent political developments in Latvia. Advertisement “The elections in Latvia were won by a coalition led by [Prime Minister] Andris Kulbergs, which seeks to maintain sanctions against Belarus. So Belarus uses both carrots and sticks to show it can destabilise the situation in the Baltics,” said Marta Jaroszewicz, assistant professor at the University of Warsaw’s Centre of Migration Research. “For the past year, there have been periodic releases of Belarusian political prisoners, a process supported by the US administration. Belarus’s goal is the lifting of sanctions and the ability to transport its raw materials via Baltic ports, including through Poland. The objective is, in fact, the normalisation of trade.” Russian and Belarusian pressure on the EU has also changed over the years as migration pressure is only one of the tactics employed. Others include disinformation, arson, the recruitment of local citizens and GPS jamming, according to Nikers. He said that “2026 is increasingly about airspace and infrastructure. The most important change is that Russia has moved from targeting what we believe to targeting what we depend on: cables, grids, navigation and airspace. It is also increasingly operating below the Article 5 threshold.” Established in the aftermath of World War II, NATO’s collective defence commitment, Article 5, was designed to ensure mutual protection among member states in response to the perceived threat of Soviet expansion, particularly in Eastern Europe during the early stages of the Cold War. “This is an attempt at intimidation by Russia. And what deters Russia from aggressive actions on the eastern flank is the solidarity of European nations,” Chmielewski said. “That is what Russia fears most: that should it stage a more brazen provocation, solidarity will stretch from Lisbon to Stockholm, and the European Union will act as a united front.”

https://www.economica.net/incendiu-la-ce.text: Home - Extern - Incendiu la cel mai mare zăcământ de gaze din lume, South Pars, din Iran Autoritățile din Iran au anunţat că au reuşit să izoleze incendiul ce a izbucnit la platforma offshore ce face parte din Faza 14 a zăcământului South Pars. Incendiul a fost stins în scurt timp, conform oficialilor companiei Pars Oil and Gas citaţi de Al Jazeera . 17 muncitori ce se aflau pe platformă în momentul izbucnirii incendiului au sărit în apă. Toţi cei 17 muncitori sunt în siguranţă, după ce au fost recuperaţi din apă de bărcile de salvare și ambarcațiuni de intervenție. O scurgere de gaze sau o eroare a celor ce oprează platforma ar putea fi cauza producerii incendiului, cred oficialii. Platforma care a luat foc contribuie cu doar 14,5 milioane de metri cubi la producția zilnică totală a zăcământului South Pars, care depășește 700 de milioane de metri cubi de gaze. South Pars/North Dome este cel mai mare zăcământ de gaze naturale din lume, situat în Golful Persic, împărțit între Iran (South Pars) și Qatar (North Dome). Acesta acoperă o suprafață totală de 9.700 kmp, din care 3.700 kmp se află în apele teritoriale iraniene. Are rezerve de aproximativ 51 de trilioane de metri cubi de gaz (cca. 19% din rezervele mondiale) și 50 de miliarde de barili de condensat. South Pars furnizează peste 70% din necesarul de gaz al Iranului, cu o capacitate de extracție ce depășește 700 de milioane mc/zi. În acest proiect au fost investite peste 80 de miliarde de dolari.
